deep_dive_html:
The Peril of the Unrestricted Guarantee

For dental practitioners, the personal guarantee is often the most significant risk in a commercial lease. Landlords frequently insist on an "unrestricted" or "unlimited" personal guarantee, which effectively pierces the corporate veil of your LLC or Professional Corporation. Under such a clause, if your practice faces insolvency or a relocation, the landlord can pursue your personal bank accounts, real estate holdings, and other non-business assets to satisfy the remaining rent obligations for the entire lease term.

The danger lies in the "continuing" nature of these guarantees. A poorly drafted clause does not just cover current rent; it covers all future obligations, including common area maintenance (CAM) escalations, tax increases, and even legal fees incurred during an eviction. This creates a massive, unquantifiable liability that can haunt a dentist long after the practice has ceased operations.

Strategic Mitigation Strategies

An elite negotiation focuses on converting an unlimited guarantee into a "Good Guy" clause or a "Limited" guarantee. The goal is to ensure that your personal liability terminates upon a specific, controlled event. Effective protections include:

    The Good Guy Clause: This limits your personal liability to the period you occupy the premises, provided you surrender the space in "broom clean" condition and pay all rent due up to the surrender date.

    The Burn-Off Provision: A clause that stipulates the personal guarantee expires entirely after a set period, such as 36 or 48 months of continuous, timely payments.

    Defined Surrender Obligations: Explicitly stating that the guarantee ends upon the delivery of keys and a formal notice of vacancy, preventing the landlord from claiming "holdover" liabilities.

Negotiating these terms requires more than just a request; it requires the precise legal language that landlords and their counsel will recognize as a standard industry compromise.
